svg.aria-label: Diagram of a role's two policies. On the left the permissions policy defines what the role may do; on the right the trust policy, a required resource-based policy, defines who may become it. Below, four forms of the Principal element and what each one actually delegates: naming an account delegates to every principal in that account present and future; naming a role ARN is transformed to a principal ID and breaks if the role is deleted and recreated; naming a service principal trusts the service acting for whoever configured it; naming a federated provider trusts anyone that identity provider issues a token for. At the bottom, the condition keys that narrow each case.
svg.title: The two halves of an IAM role, what each form of the Principal element delegates, and the conditions that narrow it
svg.text: A role is two policies, and only one of them is reviewed
The permissions policy answers what. The trust policy answers who, and it is the one that decides whether the question is ever asked.
Permissions policy — what the role may do
Identity-based. Reviewed, diffed, argued over in pull requests.
Bounded by the permissions boundary and the SCP above it.
Trust policy — who may become the role
A required resource-based policy, attached to the role itself.
Written once at onboarding. Rarely opened again.
What each form of Principal actually delegates
Delegates to the whole account. Any principal an admin there grants it to, now or in five years. You are trusting their IAM.
"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/app"
Transformed to the role's principal ID on save. Delete and recreate that role and the trust silently stops applying.
"Service": "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"
Trusts the service, not the person who configured it. Without a source condition, anyone's trail can point at your bucket.
"Federated": "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:oidc-provider/tokens.actions.githubusercontent.com"
Trusts every token that provider issues. Without a sub condition, that is every repository on the platform.
The Condition block is the actual control surface
sts:ExternalId for a third party · aws:SourceArn and aws:SourceAccount for a service · aws:PrincipalOrgID for your own accounts · the sub claim for OIDC
The Principal element names a set. The Condition block is what makes that set smaller than the whole account, the whole service, or the whole provider.
